---
title: "Growth despite decaying eigenvalues"
date: '2026-11-22'
image: nonnormal.png
categories:
- numerical-analysis
- linear-algebra
---

Consider the linear system of ODEs $u'(t) = Au(t)$, where $A$ is a $2\times 2$
matrix with real, negative eigenvalues $\lambda_1 = -1$ and $\lambda_2 \le
\lambda_1$.  Every solution decays to zero as $t\to\infty$.  But does
$\|u(t)\|$ decrease?  Only if the eigenvectors of $A$ are orthogonal (that is,
if $A$ is *normal*).  Otherwise the solution can grow, possibly by a large
factor, before it decays.

To see why, let $r_1, r_2$ be unit eigenvectors of $A$, let $R = [r_1\ r_2]$,
and write the initial value as $u(0) = z_1 r_1 + z_2 r_2$, where
$z = R^{-1}u(0)$.  Then

$$
u(t) = z_1 e^{\lambda_1 t} r_1 + z_2 e^{\lambda_2 t} r_2 .
$$

Each component (blue and green arrows below) shrinks in time.  But if the
eigenvectors are nearly parallel, then representing $u(0)$ requires large
components with opposite directions that nearly cancel.  The faster component
decays first, the cancellation is lost, and what is left is the large slower
component.  The amount of growth is limited by the condition number of the
eigenvector matrix:

$$
\|u(t)\| \le \kappa(R)\, e^{\lambda_1 t}\, \|u(0)\|, \qquad
\kappa(R) = \|R\|\,\|R^{-1}\| = \cot(\alpha/2),
$$

where $\alpha$ is the angle between the eigenvectors and the norms are
Euclidean norms.  When $\alpha = 90^\circ$, $\kappa(R) = 1$ and the solution
never grows.

The controls below set $\alpha$, the direction $\psi$ of the initial value
$u(0) = (\cos\psi, \sin\psi)$ (both in degrees), and $\lambda_2$.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof alphaDeg = Inputs.range([2, 90], {value: 15, step: 1, label: tex`\alpha`})
viewof psiDeg = Inputs.range([0, 180], {value: 60, step: 1, label: tex`\psi`})
viewof lambda2 = Inputs.range([-50, -1], {value: -10, step: 0.5, label: tex`\lambda_2`})
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
// Exact solution u(t) = z1 e^{l1 t} r1 + z2 e^{l2 t} r2, with unit eigenvectors
// r1, r2 placed symmetrically about the x-axis at angle alpha.
sys = {
  const l1 = -1, l2 = lambda2;
  const a = alphaDeg * Math.PI / 360;   // half the angle between eigenvectors
  const r1 = [Math.cos(a), Math.sin(a)], r2 = [Math.cos(a), -Math.sin(a)];
  const psi = psiDeg * Math.PI / 180, u0 = [Math.cos(psi), Math.sin(psi)];
  // Solve R z = u0 for R = [r1 r2].
  const det = r1[0] * r2[1] - r2[0] * r1[1];
  const z1 = (u0[0] * r2[1] - r2[0] * u0[1]) / det;
  const z2 = (r1[0] * u0[1] - u0[0] * r1[1]) / det;
  const parts = t => {
    const c1 = z1 * Math.exp(l1 * t), c2 = z2 * Math.exp(l2 * t);
    const p1 = [c1 * r1[0], c1 * r1[1]];
    return {p1, u: [p1[0] + c2 * r2[0], p1[1] + c2 * r2[1]]};
  };
  const ts = d3.range(0, tMax + 1e-9, 0.005);
  const path = ts.map(t => { const {u} = parts(t); return {t, x: u[0], y: u[1], norm: Math.hypot(u[0], u[1])}; });
  const kappa = 1 / Math.tan(a);
  const L = 1.1 * Math.max(1, Math.abs(z1), Math.abs(z2), d3.max(path, d => Math.max(Math.abs(d.x), Math.abs(d.y))));
  return {l1, l2, r1, r2, u0, z1, z2, parts, ts, path, kappa, L};
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
tMax = 3  // final time shown; kept separate so that changing a slider doesn't reset the time control
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof tNow = {
  const n = 300, dt = tMax / n;
  const form = html`<div style="display: flex; align-items: center; gap: .75rem; flex-wrap: wrap">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-sm btn-outline-secondary" style="min-width: 4.5rem">Play</button>
    <input type="range" min="0" max="${n}" step="1" value="0" style="flex: 1; min-width: 10rem">
    <output style="min-width: 5rem"></output></div>`;
  const [button, range, output] = form.querySelectorAll("button, input, output");
  let timer = null;
  const show = i => { form.value = i * dt; output.value = `t = ${(i * dt).toFixed(2)}`; };
  const stop = () => { clearInterval(timer); timer = null; button.textContent = "Play"; };
  range.oninput = () => show(+range.value);  // the input event then bubbles to the form
  button.onclick = () => {
    if (timer) return stop();
    if (+range.value >= n) range.value = 0;
    button.textContent = "Pause";
    timer = setInterval(() => {
      range.value = +range.value + 1;
      show(+range.value);
      form.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", {bubbles: true}));
      if (+range.value >= n) stop();
    }, 30);
  };
  invalidation.then(() => clearInterval(timer));
  show(0);
  return form;
}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{
  const {r1, r2, L, path, parts, u0} = sys;
  const {p1, u} = parts(tNow);
  const blue = "#1f77b4", green = "#2ca02c";
  const circle = d3.range(0, 2 * Math.PI + 0.01, 0.02).map(s => [Math.cos(s), Math.sin(s)]);
  const phase = Plot.plot({
    width: 360, height: 360, marginLeft: 40, marginBottom: 30,
    x: {domain: [-L, L], label: null}, y: {domain: [-L, L], label: null},
    marks: [
      Plot.ruleX([0], {strokeOpacity: 0.2}), Plot.ruleY([0], {strokeOpacity: 0.2}),
      // eigenvector directions
      Plot.line([[-L * r1[0], -L * r1[1]], [L * r1[0], L * r1[1]]], {stroke: blue, strokeOpacity: 0.4, strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
      Plot.line([[-L * r2[0], -L * r2[1]], [L * r2[0], L * r2[1]]], {stroke: green, strokeOpacity: 0.4, strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
      // unit circle: ||u|| = ||u(0)||
      Plot.line(circle, {strokeOpacity: 0.3}),
      Plot.line(path, {x: "x", y: "y", strokeOpacity: 0.5}),
      Plot.arrow([{x1: 0, y1: 0, x2: p1[0], y2: p1[1]}], {x1: "x1", y1: "y1", x2: "x2", y2: "y2", stroke: blue, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.arrow([{x1: p1[0], y1: p1[1], x2: u[0], y2: u[1]}], {x1: "x1", y1: "y1", x2: "x2", y2: "y2", stroke: green, strokeWidth: 2.5}),
      Plot.dot([u0], {x: d => d[0], y: d => d[1], r: 4, stroke: "currentColor"}),
      Plot.dot([u], {x: d => d[0], y: d => d[1], r: 5, fill: "currentColor"})
    ]
  });
  const ref = path.map(d => ({t: d.t, normal: Math.exp(sys.l1 * d.t), bound: sys.kappa * Math.exp(sys.l1 * d.t)}));
  const nNow = Math.hypot(u[0], u[1]);
  const ymax = 1.05 * Math.max(1, d3.max(path, d => d.norm));
  const norms = Plot.plot({
    width: 360, height: 360, marginLeft: 40, marginBottom: 30,
    x: {domain: [0, tMax], label: "t"},
    y: {domain: [0, ymax], label: "‖u(t)‖", grid: true},
    marks: [
      Plot.line(ref, {x: "t", y: "bound", strokeDasharray: "2,3", strokeOpacity: 0.7, clip: true}),
      Plot.line(ref, {x: "t", y: "normal", strokeDasharray: "6,4", strokeOpacity: 0.7}),
      Plot.line(path, {x: "t", y: "norm", strokeWidth: 2}),
      Plot.ruleX([tNow], {strokeOpacity: 0.3}),
      Plot.dot([{t: tNow, n: nNow}], {x: "t", y: "n", r: 5, fill: "currentColor"})
    ]
  });
  return html`<div style="display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 1rem; align-items: flex-start">
    <div>${phase}<div style="font-size: .85rem">The solution ${tex`u(t)`} (filled dot), the initial value ${tex`u(0)`} (open dot), and the components of ${tex`u(t)`}
      along the eigenvectors (<span style="color: ${blue}">blue</span>: ${tex`z_1 e^{\lambda_1 t} r_1`};
      <span style="color: ${green}">green</span>: ${tex`z_2 e^{\lambda_2 t} r_2`}).
      The circle is ${tex`\|u\| = \|u(0)\|`}.</div></div>
    <div>${norms}<div style="font-size: .85rem">Solid: ${tex`\|u(t)\|`}.
      Dashed: ${tex`e^{\lambda_1 t}`}, the most that ${tex`\|u(t)\|`} could be if the eigenvectors were orthogonal.
      Dotted: the bound ${tex`\kappa(R) e^{\lambda_1 t}`}.</div></div>
  </div>`;
}
```

Things to try:

- Press Play and watch how the green component shrinks quickly, leaving the
  long blue one.
- Make $\alpha$ smaller.  The eigenvectors become more nearly parallel and the
  growth becomes larger.
- Set $\alpha = 90^\circ$.  Now $A$ is symmetric and $\|u(t)\|$ only decreases.
- Change the direction of $u(0)$.  Initial values along one of the
  eigenvectors don't grow, and those close to one grow very little.
- Move $\lambda_2$ toward $\lambda_1$.  When the two components decay at
  similar rates, the cancellation persists and there is less growth.

The same mechanism lies behind the transient growth of powers of non-normal
matrices, which matters in the stability analysis of numerical methods, and
behind transient amplification in fluid flows whose linearizations have only
decaying modes.  A good reference is the book *Spectra and Pseudospectra* by
Trefethen and Embree.

This page is based on a
[Jupyter notebook](https://github.com/ketch/ODE-counterexamples/blob/master/Vinograd-Dekker-Verwer.ipynb)
that goes on to a more surprising example, due to Vinograd: if $A$ depends on
time, the solution can grow without bound even though the eigenvalues of
$A(t)$ are negative constants.
